synopsis: T. M. Ruff’s NIOSH work spans Report 9652, published in May 2000, a 2006 haul-truck radar study and companion accident paper, and Report 9672 from 2007 [f7983, f5173, f3064, f3060]. The 2007 report counted 22 blind-area fatalities from 2000 to mid-2006, with 67% of victims behind reversing equipment; the 2006 paper reported five blind-area fatalities annually and 12% of all surface-mine and quarry fatalities during 1999–2003 [f3060, f3062, f3064, f3065]. These historical findings establish severe blind-zone and equipment-size hazards, but should not be treated as a 2026 fatality rate; the reported dump-truck shares of 38% and 58% concern different periods and measures [f3069, f3068, f3061, f3066]. The booklet identifies Ruff’s 2006 radar study on a 260 t Caterpillar 793B as its best hard false-alarm figure: over seven days and 618 reversals, 580 alarms comprised 102 false alarms, 243 nuisance alarms and 235 actionable alarms, reported as 41% [f5173, f5174, f5436]. Nuisance alarms were valid detections without urgent danger, berm detections were excluded from that count, and staged target tests would not have exposed the operational proportion of actionable alarms; nevertheless, the Morenci trial reported false alarms insufficiently frequent to cause operators to ignore the system [f3271, f3349, f14242, f7001]. Ruff also found rear-tyre detection gaps with a single radar, improved coverage using two antennas about 1.8 m apart with beams crossed inward about 20 degrees, and one antenna failure after approximately six months of continuous vibration exposure [f7039, f7040, f7465].
